newsitem.title: KENYA: Bashir in Kenya on first trip since Sudan offensive.
newsitem.headline: Bashir in Kenya on first trip since Sudan offensive.

text.p: Sudanese President Omar Hassan al-Bashir arrived for talks in Kenya on Tuesday on his first trip abroad since a rebel offensive began one month ago.
He was met at Nairobi airport by President Daniel arap Moi, one of the few important regional leaders still on speaking terms with Sudan's Islamic-backed government.
Kenyan officials said the visit was at Bashir's request and would last a few hours.
Sudan has relations ranging from bad to bellicose with Egypt, Eritrea, Ethiopia and Uganda.

It accuses the last three of direct military involvement in the rebel offensive launched in early January from the south and east by the Sudan People's Liberation Army (SPLA) and allied opposition forces.

The United States has led most Western countries in opposing Sudan's National Islamic Front (NIF) government politically on the grounds that it harbours radical Islamic groups who export their brand of revolution.
Ambassadors to Kenya from main Western countries were not present at Tuesday's arrival ceremony. Some sent their deputies and diplomatic sources denied there was a concerted snub to Bashir.

Kenya has chaired a committee of a regional group, the Inter-Governmental Authority on Development (IGADD), since 1992 to promote peace in Sudan between the Arabised north and the black African and mainly Christian south.
"The problem is that Sudan has quarrelled with all the other members of the committee, which only leaves Kenya," a senior Kenyan official told Reuters on Monday.
"We have left the door open to Sudan because we don't want to turn it into a pariah state."
The United Arab Emirates has offered to mediate in the Sudan conflict, the official Emirates news agency WAM reported.

It said President Sheikh Zaid bin Sultan al-Nahayan made the offer when he received a telephone call from Bashir on Monday night, the first direct conversation between the two leaders since the UAE president first offered to mediate in Sudan last month.

The agency said Sheikh Zaid "voiced his readiness to start mediation and dialogue between the brothers in Sudan for reconciliation and helping to put an end to fighting and send an envoy as a practical step to his highness's initiative".
It did not say whether Bashir accepted the offer.
